citation.title: No one is watching: AI service agents and the rise of unethical consumer behavior
citation.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services 94,105001; forthcoming January2027 issue, online July2026

reading.source_scope_note: Four UK Prolific vignette samples total659 retained participations: pilot94, Study1 128, Study2 241, Study3 196. No actual AI service, cash transfer or observed fraud. Several material reporting/measurement inconsistencies prevent treating the proposed mediation, accountability substitution or priming resistance as established mechanisms. Definitions remain distinguishable from these uncertain empirical claims.
access_limits: Data are available on request; no author contact, raw dataset, executable analysis, full PROCESS output, complete coefficient covariance matrix or preregistration was obtained.

The supplied12-page article includes Appendices1–2, which were fully read. Exact analyzed item counts/scoring, reliability, moral-trait preamble, exclusion flow and total recruited Ns remain unresolved.

Cited original Aquino/Reed, Bandura, Kim and other books/studies are not independently fully read or credited from this bibliography. Corrected DOI identity is not independent full-paper verification.

The LLM coding rubric is described but exact model versions/prompts, human reference labels and independent psychometric validation are not supplied. Authors explicitly disclose the use of Claude, ChatGPT and Copilot; this is not inferred from reporting errors.

study.sampling: Randomized between-subjects vignette studies on UK English-speaking Prolific residents. Retained N94,128,241,196, approximately half women, mean ages43,46,46,45. Recruitment totals, detailed exclusion criteria/counts and cross-study participant overlap not supplied.659 is retained participations, not verified unique people.
study.pilot: Human versus AI claim handler,49 versus45 participants. Main text describes lost luggage, £500 actual loss and up to£1500 compensation; Appendix1 describes stolen luggage, euros and a friend saying a doubled claim was paid. Question asks how much Sam will ask, a third-person prediction; prose interprets it as should ask, acceptability and endorsement. These outcomes are not interchangeable. Reported means726.14 versus807.49 and F(1,92)=4.24,p=.042 refer to the authors’ reported amounts, not observed fraud.
study.agent_bundle: Studies1–3 describe the human Alex responding personally and apologizing, versus an AI assistant following an automated protocol. Agent identity, warmth/personal response and attributed error source change together; this is not an isolated manipulation of moral evaluative capacity. Both are scripted descriptions, not live conversations.
study.study1: Hypothetical£1000 laptop, expected10% voucher versus30% erroneous discount, extra£200. AI intention mean5.41 SD1.67 versus human4.74 SD2.06; F(1,126)=3.99,p=.048. Measured social-judgment mediation a=−.65,b=−.54, indirect=.35[.109,.637], direct=.31,p=.34. Randomized agent package supports a conditional scenario effect, not causal identification of a nonrandom mediator or proof of full mediation.
study.study2: N241,2×2 agent package × audit/detectability description. Moral identity measured rather than randomized. AI intention mean6.56 SD2.53 versus human5.87 SD2.44 on the stated1–7 measure; the AI mean/SD is mathematically incompatible with a bounded1–7 score, even allowing the largest sample-variance correction for any n>=2. A scoring/range/transcription clarification is necessary before quantitative synthesis.
study.study2_mediation: Reported a=−.85,b=−.47 imply .3995 if they are unstandardized paths in the same simple model, while indirect=.16[.063,.280] is printed. Scaling/model differences might explain a discrepancy but are not documented. No corrected path or effect is selected. A nonsignificant direct effect and null alternative paths do not prove a unique causal mechanism.
study.moderation: A formal moderated-moderated mediation index is reported,−.25[−.58,−.01], so do not falsely say the interaction was never tested. However, Figure2 contradicts the claimed strongest low-identity/low-detectability effect: the labeled low-detectability line rises approximately.15→.26→.37 with moral identity, while high detectability falls approximately.55→.42→.30. The lowest plotted effect is at low identity/low detectability. No CIs are plotted; swapping labels or reversing theory by guesswork is unwarranted.
study.study3: N196,agent package × autobiographical negative-evaluation prime versus typical-day writing. Prime content is classified with three LLMs; Fleiss kappa=.534, pairwise ChatGPT/Claude agreement86.2%, majority classification versus condition accuracy81.6%. Detecting expected language in a prompted narrative is not proof the specific service-agent evaluation perception was successfully manipulated. Vendor count is not guaranteed independent measurement.
study.study3_results: Intention agent effect F(1,193)=3.31,p=.070; social-judgment means human-control3.16,AI-control1.65,human-prime3.07,AI-prime1.41, consistent with Figure3. The reported social-judgment F(1,193)=18.02 implies partial eta-squared .0854, incompatible with reported eta-squared .220 for that same test. Several2×2 tests use residualdf193 instead of the192 expected for a complete interaction model on196 observations; exact model specification is needed.
study.priming_inference: Agent×prime interaction for perceived judgment p=.556, binary-choice interaction p=.470; binary agent p=.429 and prime p=.360. The binary question is another hypothetical would-do response, not a paid behavioral task. Nonsignificance does not establish cognitive immutability, intervention ineffectiveness, equivalence or corroborated agent effects on actual misconduct. No equivalence margin, precise null interval or complete power rationale is supplied.
study.intentions_measure: Methods say four unethical-intention items; Appendix2 supplies three: own willingness, moral acceptability and what most others would do. This combines intention, normative appraisal and a descriptive norm. Scoring, missing fourth item and reliability are not specified. All stated measures use seven-point scales; a summed scoring explanation cannot be silently assumed to repair Study2.
study.judgment_measure: Theoretical definition concerns an agent’s perceived moral-evaluative capacity, while the three items ask anxiety/fear/worry about a negative impression. Capacity attribution, evaluative concern, felt accountability and actual monitoring are related but distinct; no unique moral-audience mechanism is isolated.
study.identity_measure: Appendix2 mixes three self-importance items and three outward-expression/product/hobby items, without listing the referred-to moral characteristics. It does not clearly isolate internalized identity from symbolic expression. Measured identity moderation is not a causal personality effect or a basis to infer dishonesty from anonymity.
study.alternative_mechanisms: Entitlement and moral disengagement indirect CIs include zero, which fails to establish their irrelevance. Anticipatory guilt is discussed as an alternative but no guilt measure appears among the reported items; it cannot be declared ruled out. Study1 entitlement path product also depends on coefficient/model scaling details not supplied.
study.design_implications: Human oversight, hybrid agents, anthropomorphism, monitoring systems and moral-identity targeting are proposed rather than tested interventions. The audit-description manipulation changes perceived detectability, not actual detection. Do not justify covert surveillance, fake human observers or moral profiling from the supplied evidence.
study.ethics: NOVA IMS ethics code DDMKT2024-10-38318 and informed consent are reported. The identifier alone does not identify the actual approval date or recruitment dates. Statistical inconsistencies do not prove fabricated data, malicious intent or undisclosed generative-AI use.

study2_AI_unethical_intention.interpretation: Even the most permissive n/(n−1) correction cannot reconcile this pair on a1–7 bounded score. A different scoring rule, range or transcription must be clarified; no corrected SD is invented.

study3_social_judgment.interpretation: For this single-df F test, partial eta squared is about.0854. Ordinary eta squared cannot exceed it in the same ANOVA; the reported.220 needs clarification.

study2_simple_mediation.interpretation: If coefficients are unstandardized paths from the same simple model, the product should be.3995. Scaling or model differences are not documented; do not choose a repaired value.

study3_binary_choice.interpretation: No reported term reaches significance; this does not corroborate a detected agent effect on the binary hypothetical choice, nor establish equivalence.

summary: Add perceived social judgment, moral identity and moral self-regulation as clearly scoped human constructs, not established harmful AI mechanisms. Preserve the empirical reporting concerns, unsuccessful binary-choice detection and noncausal mediation limits. Correct a truncated source DOI and author spelling; retain the verified forthcoming2027 issue/2026 availability distinction.

findings.definition: Perceiving an interaction partner as capable of socially or morally evaluating one’s conduct.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human construct defined in a vignette study with material reporting limitations; proposed AI analogue not tested
findings.novelty_rationale: A distinct construct absent from the retained names, synonyms and definitions; related feelings, attribution, disengagement and self-presentation are linked rather than treated as synonyms.

evidence.quote: defined as the extent to which consumers feel evaluated by an entity

findings.evidence_scope: The article explicitly defines perceived social judgment and studies it using three negative-impression concern items. Those ratings differ between scripted human/AI conditions, but scale-content, mediation, plotting and summary-statistic issues materially limit the claimed causal mechanism.
findings.boundary: Being capable of evaluating, worrying about evaluation, actually being monitored, moral agency and warranted accountability differ. This is not strategic model sandbagging, general social presence or proof that AI cannot evaluate evidence. No machine subjective judgment or human feeling is inferred from model text.
findings.ai_proposal: Test truthful source and review-process disclosures in assistance workflows while measuring perceived evaluation separately from actual detection capability. Check whether outputs change with legitimate oversight; never simulate a human observer or claimed emotion merely to induce compliance.

findings.definition: The importance of moral qualities to a person’s self-concept.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human construct defined in a vignette study with material reporting limitations; proposed AI analogue not tested
findings.novelty_rationale: A distinct construct absent from the retained names, synonyms and definitions; related feelings, attribution, disengagement and self-presentation are linked rather than treated as synonyms.

evidence.quote: concept is rooted in moral domains

findings.evidence_scope: The theory section defines moral identity as moral self-concept importance, citing Aquino/Reed2002. The study uses a six-item adaptation mixing internal self-importance and outward expression; its moderated-mediation account remains uncertain and is not a causal identity manipulation.
findings.boundary: Moral self-importance does not establish ethically justified conduct, superior moral worth or a clinical trait diagnosis. Internalization and signaling differ. A model’s moral self-description or an anonymous user’s profile does not demonstrate moral identity or dishonesty.
findings.ai_proposal: Evaluate whether explicit ethical commitments consistently constrain a model’s decisions across matched contexts and pressures, separating observable consistency from self-praise or a claim to possess a moral self.

findings.definition: Monitoring and adjusting one’s conduct against internalized moral standards.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human construct defined in a vignette study with material reporting limitations; proposed AI analogue not tested
findings.novelty_rationale: A distinct construct absent from the retained names, synonyms and definitions; related feelings, attribution, disengagement and self-presentation are linked rather than treated as synonyms.

evidence.quote: evaluate their actions against internalized moral standards

findings.evidence_scope: The theory section defines ongoing self-monitoring against moral standards, citing Bandura1991. The experiments propose that social evaluation triggers restraint, but do not directly observe a complete self-regulation process or demonstrate that AI uniquely removes it.
findings.boundary: Self-monitoring, externally imposed control, moral disengagement, guilt and successful ethical conduct differ. Internalized standards can be mistaken. Generated reflection is not proof of a model’s conscience, feelings or durable self-directed learning.
findings.ai_proposal: Test whether an assistant checks proposed actions against explicit ethical constraints, detects mismatches and makes justified corrections across steps, using independent outcomes rather than accepting its self-report of being ethical.

findings.definition: Suspending or bypassing moral self-regulation so harmful conduct can be justified before or after it occurs.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain an existing construct and add contrary/limited evidence or a non-counting boundary, without a duplicate label.
findings.evidence_scope: Study2 measures a three-item adaptation focused on blame/justification and reports an indirect interval including zero. This is limited contrary/uncertain evidence for a mediation route, not demonstration that moral disengagement is absent.
findings.boundary: A few adapted blame items do not exhaust the construct. Null indirect effects do not rule out a mechanism, and moral disengagement differs from merely feeling less judged. Unresolved scoring/statistical problems preclude strong quantitative synthesis.

findings.definition: Expecting to feel guilty about a contemplated action or omission that would violate one’s moral standards.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain an existing construct and add contrary/limited evidence or a non-counting boundary, without a duplicate label.

evidence.quote: rather than by entitlement, anticipatory guilt,

findings.evidence_scope: Anticipatory guilt is discussed as an earlier explanation, but the reported current measures do not include a guilt scale. The paper does not independently test away that mechanism.
findings.boundary: Expected guilt, negative-evaluation concern, moral identity and blame justification differ. Bibliography discussion is not a measured null or independent full-paper credit; this boundary does not fill a supporting-paper gap.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Mean6.56,SD2.53 cannot describe a1–7 bounded score as stated. Different item scoring, range, sample or transcription is possible, but no repaired value is asserted.

The labeled conditional-effect curves contradict the strongest low-identity/low-detectability narrative. Their positive/negative slopes and detectability ordering cannot be reconciled by simply assuming the theory is right; original model output and plotting code are needed.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: PDF pages5–6 and8, mediation/effect size/model df
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Study2 path product does not match the stated indirect effect under a common unstandardized simple model. Study3 F/eta-squared and several residualdf/model descriptions also require clarification. Conditional mathematical checks are retained without inventing raw-data corrections.

Methods say four items; Appendix2 supplies three spanning willingness, acceptability and a descriptive norm. Obtain actual analyzed items, aggregation rule and reliability before pooling this as a homogeneous intention measure.

Lost luggage/pounds in procedures differ from stolen luggage/euros plus a peer example in Appendix1. The question predicts what Sam will request, while prose treats it as approval. Actual presented stimuli and interpretation need clarification.

The four-item self-control block cites Campbell2004, whose listed paper validates psychological entitlement. The exact self-control instrument source is not identified here; do not silently replace it with a guessed source.

methodological_limits: Vignettes and hypothetical outcomes, no real money or autonomous AI service. Agent descriptions bundle social/personal response and automated protocol.
Measured mediators and identity are not randomized; null alternatives and nonsignificant direct effects do not prove full or unique causal mediation.
Material scale/statistic/plot conflicts prevent reliable quantitative synthesis of several key claims. Narrative labels must not replace raw-data verification.
Null priming effects and hypothetical binary choices do not establish an immutable structural mechanism, equivalent outcomes or an effective field intervention.
No original recruitment/exclusion flow, independent LLM psychometric validation or full scoring/reliability details. No basis for inferred moral profiling or actual consumer misconduct prevalence.

cross_paper_learning.finding: As with the sentencing figures, inspect labels against text and data. Here no public raw workbook was obtained, so the moderation-plot conflict cannot be repaired and inferential results cannot be fully reproduced.
Conflicting or impossible summary statistics require explicit disclosure, not selection of the preferred table/claim. Date validity and source existence are separate from empirical reporting quality.
The authors do test interactions, but nulls do not establish practical equivalence or a unique structural explanation. Study3’s binary agent effect is also undetected.
Immediate consumer expectations and prompted hypothetical decisions do not test later human–human transfer, lasting value change or actual machine feeling.

deferred.reason: A manipulated contextual cue and a disputed conditional mechanism; do not add a new behavior solely from a moderator label or unresolved plot.
Relevant but the exact self-control source and narrower negative-evaluation instrument require original-source review before separate new entries.
Overstated effect/mechanism labels; intention, forecast, acceptability and actual misconduct differ, and nulls do not identify immutability.

deferred.term: Psychological entitlement as a standalone new entry
deferred.reason: A named control/alternative route with insufficient reviewed conceptual definition here; source identification alone is not full-original reading.

limitations: Three new human constructs, not three validated harmful AI mechanisms. Source definitions are retained separately from contested empirical effects; no extra unread-source credit, fabricated timeline counts, automatic harm/principle edges, actual-fraud claim or model-consciousness inference.
